Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:1.english: Reading a book - All their books were made like a scroll.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:10.english: And behold, it did not come to rest - And why is it forbidden to roll it [back] to himself?

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:2.english: And the book rolled from his hand - And one of its ends [was] in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:3.hebrew: גוללו אצלו - ובפרק בתרא דעירובין מוקים לה באיסקופת כרמלית — כגון גבוה ג' ורחבו ד', ורשות הרבים עוברת לפניו — דאי נפל כוליה מידיה ומהדרי ליה מרה"ר לאיסקופה, לאו חיוב חטאת איכא. הלכך, השתא דראשו אחד בידו ואין כאן עקירה, אפילו משום שבות נמי לא גזור:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:3.english: He rolls it [back] to himself - And in the last chapter of Eruvin [98a], [the Gemara] establishes it [as dealing with] a threshold that is a karmelit — such as [where it is] three [handbreadths] high and four [handbreadths] wide, and the public domain passes in front of it — for if the entire [scroll] were to fall from his hand and he were to bring it back from the public domain to the threshold, there is no liability for a sin-offering. Therefore, now that one of its ends is in his hand and there is no uprooting here, [the Sages] did not decree even a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:4.english: [If] he was reading on top of the roof - Which is a private domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:5.english: And the book rolled from his hand - And one of its ends [is] in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:6.english: Before it reached - The lower end [of the scroll].

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:7.hebrew: לי' - התחתונים, שהוא אויר ר"ה — גוללו אצלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:7.english: To ten - The lowest [ten handbreadths], which is the airspace of the public domain — he may roll it back to himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:8.hebrew: הגיע לי' - אסור לגוללו, דגזור רבנן משום שבות היכא דאוגדו בידו אטו היכא דנפק מידיה כוליה, דלא לייתיה, דאיכא חיובא דאורייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:8.english: [Once] it reached [within] ten [handbreadths] - It is forbidden to roll it [back to himself], for the Sages decreed a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] in a case where its end is [held] in his hand on account of a case where it completely slipped from his hand, so that he will not bring it [back], as there is a Torah liability [in that case].

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:9.hebrew: הופכו על הכתב - כתבו לצד הכותל, והחלק כלפי ר"ה, שלא יהא מוטל כל כך בבזיון:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:1:9.english: He turns it over onto the writing - Its writing [facing] toward the wall and the blank [side] toward the public domain, so that it will not lie in such disgrace.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:2:1.hebrew: משופע - בולט מלמטה ומצר מלמעלה, דנח ליה על אותו שיפוע:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:2:1.english: Inclined - Protruding at the bottom and narrowing at the top, so that [the scroll] rests upon that incline.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:2:2.english: Is [water] wont to come to rest - [It does not,] except in something that has an interior.

Rashi on Shabbat 5b:3:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - לאו היינו הנחתן דתהוי עקירתו עקירה, דהא ניידי ואזלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 5b:3:1.english: Lest you say - [That] this is not their placement, such that his lifting would be [a valid] lifting, for they are moving and flowing away.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5b:1:1.hebrew: היה קורא בספר על האסקופה - ואם תאמר: ולרבא בפרקין, דלא גזר בכרמלית גזירה לגזירה גבי "לא יצא החייט במחטו" (לקמן יא:), מאי איריא ספר? אפילו כל מילי נמי שרי באגדו בידו, כיון דאפילו באין אגדו בידו לא אסור אלא מדרבנן, ואי אפשר לאוקמה אלא באסקופת כרמלית, כדמסיק אביי בפרק בתרא דעירובין (ד צח. ושש)! וי"ל, דנקט ספר לאשמעינן: אפילו ספר, אם אין אגודו בידו — אסור, לאפוקי רבי שמעון, דאמר התם: "כל דבר שהוא משום שבות אינו עומד בפני כתבי הקודש":
Tosafot on Shabbat 5b:1:1.english: "One who was reading a scroll on the threshold" - And if you say: According to Rava in our chapter, who does not issue a decree upon a decree in [the case of] a karmelit, regarding "A tailor may not go out with his needle" (below, 11b) — why [speak] specifically of a scroll? Even any other item should also be permitted when its end is held in one's hand, since even when its end is not in one's hand, it is forbidden only rabbinically, and it is impossible to explain [the Mishnah] other than [as referring to] a threshold that is a karmelit, as Abaye concludes in the final chapter of Eruvin (98a, and ibid.)! And it can be answered: [The Mishnah] mentioned a scroll to teach us that even [in the case of] a scroll, if its end is not in one's hand, it is forbidden — to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Shimon, who said there: "Anything that is [prohibited] on account of a shevut [a rabbinic decree] does not stand before sacred writings."

Tosafot on Shabbat 5b:2:1.hebrew: בכותל משופע - אור"י, דאיירי כגון שרבים מכתפים עליו, דהוי רה"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 5b:2:1.english: "In [the case of] an inclined wall" - The Ri explains that it is dealing with [a case] such as where the public adjusts their loads upon it, so that it is [considered] a public domain.
